definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 12 months, as of the analysis date.
formula_or_rule: max(order_date) >= current_date - 365 over orders with status <> 'cancelled' (pending/shipped/delivered/returned count; cancelled does not)
example: On 2026-11-25, last order 2026-01-10 (delivered) = active; last order 2025-10-01 = not active
notes_conflicts: Conflict settled: Sales wanted 6 months, Finance 12 months (investors compare years). Finance definition adopted company-wide; Sales uses the separate term recently_active_customer for its 6-month view.

definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 6 months; the Sales/marketing segment.
formula_or_rule: max(order_date) >= current_date - 183 over orders with status <> 'cancelled'
example: On 2026-11-25, last order 2026-06-01 = recently active; last order 2026-02-01 = not (but still active)
notes_conflicts: New term created to give Sales its 6-month view without redefining active customer (one term = one definition).

definition_one_sentence: What ShopFast really keeps on an order: gross revenue minus refunds, excluding VAT, shipping fees included.
formula_or_rule: net_revenue_eur = round((total_amount_eur - refunds) / 1.20, 2) with French VAT 20%
notes_conflicts: Conflict settled: Finance excludes VAT (VAT is not our money), Sales wanted VAT-included (commissions). VAT-included amount = gross_revenue; Sales must not redefine net revenue.

definition_one_sentence: A customer who is not active anymore: no non-cancelled order in the last 12 months.
formula_or_rule: last_order_date < current_date - 365 OR last_order_date IS NULL (with signup_date older than 12 months)
example: On 2026-11-25, last order 2025-10-01 = churned; the churn-prediction model scores customers at risk of becoming churned
notes_conflicts: Direct negation of active customer; no ambiguity on cancelled orders (they never keep a customer active).

definition_one_sentence: A purchase transaction placed by a customer on the ShopFast site in one go, identified by a unique order_id, whatever its status.
formula_or_rule: One row in fct_orders per order_id; statuses pending → shipped → delivered, or returned / cancelled; cancelled generates no revenue, returned is removed from net revenue via refunds
notes_conflicts: Statuses are normalized in stg_orders ('canceled' → 'cancelled', casing/trailing spaces trimmed).

definition_one_sentence: A person who created an account on the ShopFast site, identified by a customer_id; the same person may hold several accounts.
formula_or_rule: Counted by customer_id, one row in stg_customers / dim_customers per account, exists from signup_date onwards
example: Customer 10845, gold loyalty tier, signed up 2024 — 1233 accounts ≠ 1233 persons (duplicate emails exist)
notes_conflicts: Known quality issue: duplicate persons with several accounts; customer count is an upper bound of person count.
